category: normal valid variant (ATH on first bar)

rejection_rationale.rejected_because: Its steeper line passes below the t=10 bar high (150), which pierces beyond eps -> not envelope-valid.

rejection_rationale.candidate: tA!=0 (treating t=0 as not-anchorable because no k=3 window exists to its left)
rejection_rationale.rejected_because: The ATH bar is an anchor by construction (§4: earliest bar at the global max), independent of any pivot test (§5, §18 ATH-on-first-bar). Pivot status is non-authoritative throughout selection (§6, D-TL-03, HD-11).
rejection_rationale.numeric: HA=max H[t]=200 at t=0 (unique global max); anchor A=(0,200) accepted.

key_inequalities: Candidacy = ALL later bar highs below the ATH (§6) — NOT a pivot subset; t=5 (170) and t=10 (150) are the two competitors this fixture was designed around (both are also k=3 pivots, which is descriptive only and not a candidacy condition). See geometry_check.open_issue_2026_07_25: over the full 15-bar history the candidate set is larger than these two and the stated B* is contested.
Only (10,150) dominates every intervening high within eps; (5,170) fails on t=10.
geometry_check.notes: Demonstrates the §18 'ATH on the first bar' edge case resolves to a normal valid line, not an error. That headline behaviour (tA=0 is anchorable) is unaffected by the open issue below.

open_issue_2026_07_25.raised_by: Architect, during the Issue #16 stale-pivot sweep
open_issue_2026_07_25.status: UNRESOLVED — escalated to the Orchestrator / Product Owner. NOT decided by Issue #16; the expected geometry in this file is left UNCHANGED.
open_issue_2026_07_25.summary: With the pivot precondition removed (§6, HD-11), bars t=11..14 are eligible candidates even though none is a k=3 pivot (each is within k of the series end). The t=11 high (146) already sits ABOVE the stated A->(10,150) line (within eps, so not a pierce), which is the signature of a shallower valid candidate; the shallowest candidate over the full history is t=14 (H=135), whose line dominates every bar high with ZERO violations even at eps=0. A plain reading of §8 step 4 therefore makes B*=(14,135), not (10,150).
open_issue_2026_07_25.the_open_question: Identical to OPEN-GX15-HULL-RESELECTION in GX-15: over what window is §8 step 4 evaluated — the full history (making a near-end bar the canonical anchor) or the formation window (freezing selection at t=10)? Before HD-11 the pivot precondition answered this implicitly by excluding bars within k of the series end; HD-11 removed the exclusion without stating a replacement.
open_issue_2026_07_25.why_not_decided_here: It is a product-definition decision, and Issue #16 changes NO rule. Constraint from approved evidence: RM-01's PO-approved canonical anchor is itself only 3 bars from the end of its series, so 'exclude bars within k of the end from selection' would contradict RM-01/HD-11.
open_issue_2026_07_25.impact: fixtures/VERIFICATION.md's claim that the stated B* is the all-highs upper-log-hull vertex for 16/16 geometry fixtures does not hold for this fixture (or GX-15) when the hull search is run over the FULL history rather than the formation window.
